belief: I'm responsible for fixing my family's problems.
origins: In many families one person becomes the fixer: the capable one who steps in with money, advice, rescues, or mediation. Often it begins in childhood, when a parent was overwhelmed. Over time, the role becomes identity, and we feel guilty when we cannot solve a problem or when others do not accept our help.
teaches: Paul says, “Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ,” and in the same chapter, “each one should carry his own load.” Both are true: we help, and each person remains responsible for their life. “Each of us will give an account of himself to God.” Jesus said, “Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest… My burden is light.” The Lord is the Savior of your family. You are not.
self_statements: If I do not step in, everything will fall apart.
They need me to fix this.
I am the only responsible one.
It is my fault if they struggle.
I cannot rest until it is solved.
errors: Treating others’ problems as my responsibility.
Insisting that I should rescue everyone.
Imagining collapse if I step back.
questions: When did I become the fixer, and why?
Which problems are really mine, and which belong to others?
What happens when I rescue repeatedly?
What is the difference between helping and rescuing?
What does Jesus invite me to do with my burden?
What is one problem I can hand back or hand to God?
truth: I can help my family without being their savior. Each person carries their own load, and I can carry burdens with them in healthy ways. I can rest in Jesus, who is gentle, and trust Him with what I cannot fix.
hw_truths: Each person carries their own load.
Helping is not the same as rescuing.
I am not the Savior of my family.
I can say no to some requests.
God is able to work in their lives.
log: Each week, write one problem you handed back to its owner or to God.
actions: List family problems and mark whose they are.
Choose one problem to return kindly to its owner.
Offer listening or prayer instead of fixing.
Read it slowly and pray it.
prayer: Lord Jesus, I have tried to carry my family. I give You the burdens I cannot fix. Teach me to help with wisdom, to hand back what is theirs, and to rest in You. Amen.
hw_questions: When did I become the fixer?
How can I help without fixing?
What can I hand to God?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Each person carries their own load, and I can trust God with my family.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I'm responsible for fixing my family's problems.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
